the 2-D constitutive equations are obtained by averaging the 3-D ones over the thickness, and the 1-D equations are derived by averaging the 2-D ones over the width, with the reduced coefficients being the averages of the 3-D coefficients over thickness, width or length, and the enhanced coefficients being the averages over width, length or thickness.

the dimensional reduction from the 3D to 2D and 1D constitutive equations of piezoelectrics, and the effects on the design of macro and micro-sized devices.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the dimensional reduction of piezoelectrics leads to a decrease in stiffness and compliance and an increase in piezoelectric coefficient.

the dimensional reduction of the constitutive equation from 3-D (bulk material) to 2-D (thin plate) or 1-D (thin film) results in changes of the coefficients, and the changes depend on the device geometry and configuration.

the 2-D equations are valid for all 2-D devices, and the 1-D equations are valid only for 1-D devices with a thickness direction that coincides with the direction of the poling field, while the reduced and enhanced coefficients are valid for 2-D devices and 1-D devices, respectively.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the 2-D constitutive equations are more appropriate than the 1-D ones for the design of sensors and actuaters, and the enhanced coefficients should be preferred over the reduced ones for better performance evaluation.

the reduced coefficients are the most appropriate for use in the design and analysis, while the enhanced coefficients are useful to understand the effect of the dimensional reduction on the piezoelectrics.
